youtube.title: Every shuffle is new | Possibility Lab Season 2 · Episode 4
youtube.caption:
Has this ever happened? Shuffle a deck, and look at the order.

Fifty-two cards can be ordered in 52! ways: about 8.07 × 10^67, a number with 68 digits. Give everyone alive a deck, a shuffle a second, for 13.8 billion years, and that is about 3.6 × 10^27 shuffles: less than one part in 10^36 of all the orders. Shuffle well (about seven riffle shuffles) and your order has almost certainly never existed before.

Series: Season 2, episode 4 of 6.

Sources
1. A standard deck has 52 cards; each position can take any card not yet used (52, then 51, then 50 ...). — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
2. 52 x 51 x ... x 1 = 52! = 80,658,175,170,943,878,571,660,636,856,403,766,975,289,505,440,883,277,824,000,000,000,000 (about 8.07 x 10^67), exact integer arithmetic in calc.py. — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
3. 52! has 68 digits (log10 52! = 67.9). — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
4. World population about 8.2 billion. — population.un.org: https://population.un.org/wpp/
5. The universe began around 13.8 billion years ago ('fourteen billion' is a rounding; the sum uses 13.8). — NASA: https://science.nasa.gov/universe/overview/
6. 8.2e9 people x 13.8e9 years x 3.156e7 s = 3.6e27 shuffles; 3.6e27 / 8.07e67 = 4.4e-41, which is less than 1 part in 10^36 (a trillion trillion trillion). — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
7. If a shuffle is fair and uniform, the chance that it matches any specific earlier one is 1 in 52!; against all 3.6e27 shuffles in the thought experiment it is 4.4e-41. (The chance that any two of those ever match is about 8e-14, by the birthday bound N^2 / (2 x 52!).) — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
8. With 1,000 times the people the share is 4.4e-38: still less than 1 part in 10^36. — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
9. If a shuffle is fair and uniform, the chance that it matches any specific earlier one is 1 in 52!; against all 3.6e27 shuffles in the thought experiment it is 4.4e-41. (The chance that any two of those ever match is about 8e-14, by the birthday bound N^2 / (2 x 52!).) — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
10. About seven riffle shuffles are enough to mix a 52-card deck close to uniformly at random. — projecteuclid.org: https://projecteuclid.org/journals/annals-of-applied-probability/volume-2/issue-2/Trailing-the-Dovetail-Shuffle-to-its-Lair/10.1214/aoap/1177005705.full

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
